title: Article 124C — Power of Parliament to make law (NJAC) (Inoperative)

content.overview: Article 124C was inserted by the Constitution (Ninety-ninth Amendment) Act, 2014 as part of the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) framework, empowering Parliament to regulate appointment procedure. The Supreme Court in Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (2015) struck down the 99th Amendment (including Articles 124A–124C) and the NJAC Act as violating judicial independence (basic structure). The provision remains in some printed texts but is inoperative; the collegium system continues.
content.glance: Art 124C (NJAC) inserted by 99th Amendment 2014; struck down by SC 2015. Inoperative. Collegium continues.
content.study:
Article 124C authorised Parliament to make law regulating the procedure for appointment of the Chief Justice of India and other Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts and related NJAC matters.

Status: Inserted by the Constitution (Ninety-ninth Amendment) Act, 2014 (w.e.f. 13-4-2015). Declared unconstitutional and void by the Supreme Court in the NJAC judgment (2015). Not operative law.

Living frame: Judicial appointments continue under the collegium system as restored by that judgment.

Examination rule: State that Article 124C is inoperative after the 2015 judgment; do not treat NJAC as the current appointment mechanism.

sections.heading: Constitutional status
sections.body: Inserted by the 99th Amendment, 2014 as part of NJAC (with Arts 124A and 124B). Struck down by the Supreme Court in Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (2015) on basic-structure grounds (judicial independence). Inoperative; collegium continues.

sections.heading: Exam checkpoints
sections.body:
1. Distinguish textual presence from operative effect.
2. Cite the 2015 NJAC judgment for invalidity of the 99th Amendment package.
3. Current mechanism: collegium (Second and Third Judges cases line, reaffirmed 2015).

misconceptions.trap: NJAC under Articles 124A–124C is the current appointment system.
misconceptions.correction: The 99th Amendment and NJAC were struck down in 2015. The collegium system continues. Article 124C is inoperative.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the status of Article 124C?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 124C was inserted by the 99th Amendment, 2014 as part of NJAC. The Supreme Court struck down the 99th Amendment (including Art 124C) in 2015. The provision is inoperative; judicial appointments continue under the collegium system.

cases.name: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India
cases.holding: The 99th Constitutional Amendment and the NJAC Act were struck down as violating the basic structure (judicial independence). Articles 124A–124C are unconstitutional and inoperative.
cases.relevance: Mandatory citation for status of Art 124C / NJAC.

examTips: Always state: inserted by 99th Amendment; struck down 2015; collegium continues.
